issues.title: Unsigned powers in the arbitrary-q critical-point theorem
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims the result for every real q>1. Although the first expression defines L through the real ℓq norm, the paper expands it as sums of signed powers and differentiates it using w=R^{q-1}. Residual components, including boundary residuals u_j-g_j, are unrestricted in sign. Thus nonintegral powers may not be real, odd integral powers are not the asserted norm, and the displayed gradient identity lacks the signed duality map |R|^{q-2}R.
issues.overall_effect: The arbitrary-q unique-critical-point conclusion is not established as printed, and the same unsigned-power defect propagates to the time-dependent critical-point theorem and the stochastic loss formula. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution itself are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write every scalar contribution to the ℓq loss as |z|^q and define the duality map J_q(z)=|z|^{q-2}z, with J_q(0)=0. In the steady proof use w=J_q(R(u*)), so that ∇L=DR(u*)^T w, and make the same replacements in the time-dependent proof and sampled loss. Since J_q(z)=0 exactly when z=0, this retains the claims for every q>1.
issues.why_classification: The norm displayed in the old source itself forces the signed-power correction, but the proof's gradient vector and inference must genuinely be repaired, so this is not merely transcriptional. The repair is nevertheless standard, local, and preserves the arbitrary-q theorem, its time-dependent counterpart, and the loss guarantees without a new argument architecture.

issues.title: Invalid transposition step in the nonsmooth critical-point proof

failure_location.quote: We know from Lemma \ref{lem:DR-invertible}, that the matrix $\left(D \cR(u_n^{(k)})\right)^\top$ is $\mu$-diagonally dominant with $\mu$ independent of $n$ and $k$.

issues.failure_explanation: Each old limit A_k is defined as a limit of transposed Jacobians. Lemma lem:DR-invertible only gives row diagonal dominance for the untransposed Jacobians, so the claim that the A_k and their convex combination retain that row property is false in general. Although the combination is invertible after regrouping it as the transpose of a convex combination of untransposed Jacobians, that necessary argument is absent.
issues.overall_effect: The unique-critical-point characterization is not proved for merely Lipschitz residuals, and the time-dependent critical-point theorem's claimed analogous nonsmooth extension inherits the missing argument. The smooth case and the existence/homeomorphism argument are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take limits B_k=lim_n DR(u_n^(k)) before transposing. Then B=Σ_k α_k B_k belongs to the generalized differential of R, retains the row diagonal-dominance and sign structure, and is invertible, while stationarity reads B^T w=0. Apply the same regrouping in the analogous nonsmooth time-dependent step.
issues.why_classification: The assertion that transposition preserves row diagonal dominance is a false mathematical inference, not a typo. However, regrouping the existing terms as the transpose of a convex combination of untransposed Jacobians is a short, routine matrix argument that preserves the full steady and time-dependent conclusions.

issues.title: Missing boundary condition for the comparison solution
issues.failure_explanation: The statement purports to control u-v by the mismatch between b-bar and c-bar, but it imposes both boundary assignments on u and none on v. The proof's boundary maximum argument requires v_j=c-bar_j. Thus the argument supports the theorem with a different, corrected boundary hypothesis, not the literal printed statement.
issues.overall_effect: The steady comparison estimate is not established under its printed hypotheses, and the following a posteriori proposition cannot obtain its initial discrete bound from that statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second boundary assignment by v_j=bar c_j for j in B, use bar b_j-bar c_j consistently in the boundary maximum in the proof, and invoke this corrected estimate in the following a posteriori proposition.
issues.why_classification: The comparison norm, the two boundary data sets, and the proof's boundary-maximum argument uniquely force the missing assignment to v. The proof already follows the corrected reading, so only inconsistent variable notation must be transcribed correctly and no mathematical inference changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the literal printed definition, 1-lambda v equals 1-lambda+exp(-lambda u), not exp(-lambda u), and homogeneity does not yield H(x,∇v)+lambda f v=0 except in a special unit-parameter case. The stated inverse instead requires v=(1-exp(-lambda u))/lambda.

issues.title: Out-of-range multilevel schedule quantifier
issues.failure_explanation: For m>M, lambda^(m), alpha^(m), and Δx^(m) are undeclared; at m=2M the clause also requests level 2M+1. Conversely, the loop actually visits m=0 through M-1, while the printed Ensure clause starts at m=1. The schedule contract therefore neither covers all executed transitions nor refers only to declared levels.
issues.overall_effect: The monotonicity precondition of the multilevel algorithm is undefined on much of its stated range and omits the first transition used by the loop.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Ensure-clause range by all integers m with 0≤m<M, so each condition concerns the declared adjacent levels m and m+1 and covers every transition executed by the loop.
issues.why_classification: The declared levels 0 through M and the loop m=0 through M-1 uniquely determine the corrected index range. No schedule design or mathematical reasoning is needed beyond fixing the out-of-range quantifier.

issues.title: Inconsistent spatial dimension in the obstacle experiment

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we solve a time-dependent non-linear advection problem in $\R^5$ with a rigid obstacle.
$\mathcal{X}$ is a batch of $10^4$ points sampled uniformly at random in $(0,2)\times (-2.5, 2.5)^5$

issues.failure_explanation: The executable construction has no common input space: its PDE data are declared on Ω=[-2,2]^6 with a_0 in R^6, but its collocation samples lie in five spatial dimensions and its numerical Hamiltonians use only e_1 through e_5. Thus the printed target problem and trained residual cannot be instantiated together.
issues.overall_effect: The old obstacle experiment is dimensionally ambiguous and cannot literally be executed as the stated six-dimensional problem using its five-dimensional batches and stencils.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Present the experiment consistently as five-dimensional: set Ω=[-2,2]^5 and a_0 in R^5, replace the R^6 and N^6 prose claims by their five-dimensional versions, and retain the existing five-dimensional samples, stencils, network inputs, figures, and output.
issues.why_classification: This contained repair makes the recorded computation executable without reconstructing or rerunning it, and the same high-dimensional obstacle experiment remains recognizable. It nevertheless withdraws the coherent advertised six-dimensional model and scalability claim, which is a limited substantive loss rather than a uniquely forced typo or a no-loss minor correction.

issues.title: Drift normalization mismatch in the obstacle residual

failure_location.quote: \left( \sum_{i=1}^5 \dfrac{u(t, x+ \Delta x e_i) - u(t, x-\Delta x e_i) }{2\Delta x} \right)_+

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the direction of the drift is given by $a = \frac{a_0}{\| a_0\|} $

issues.failure_explanation: For d=5, the advertised Hamiltonian is (a·∇u)_+=(sum_i ∂_i u)_+/sqrt(5). The implemented centered and higher-order stencils use (sum_i D_i u)_+ without this factor. They therefore approximate sqrt(5) times the advertised directional Hamiltonian and train for a different propagation speed.
issues.overall_effect: The trained residual targets a different advection speed from the old PDE, so the numerical output is not an approximation of the advertised normalized-drift problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For d=5 let c=√5 and let U denote the approximation trained with the printed unnormalized drift a_0. Report V(t,x)=U(t/c,x), use time increments cΔt and the numerical Hamiltonian H_impl/c, and regenerate the snapshots by evaluating U at time t/c. Then V_t+(a·∇V)_+=c^{-1}[U_t+(a_0·∇U)_+], and positive scaling of the evolution branch leaves the obstacle condition equivalent.
issues.why_classification: The implemented residual genuinely has the wrong speed, so the defect is not a typo. Nevertheless, a fixed and routine time rescaling converts the existing computation exactly to the normalized-drift problem, including its discrete time scale and reported outputs, without retraining, changing the method, or losing the advertised guarantee.
